title: How Horseflies Bite You 😨

analysis_notes.transcript_source: YouTube auto-subs (en-orig, word-timed); 'en' track returned HTTP 429 but en-orig is the same ASR
analysis_notes.frames: sampled every 1 s (28 frames); contact sheet research/library/sheets/6mRR91AbxjQ.jpg is 7x4 tiles, row-major, 1 s per tile (tile 1 = 0 s). Shot boundaries refined from a 2 fps pass.

title_pattern.notes: 4 words + emoji. Second-person ('You') makes a nature fact personal and slightly threatening; 'How ... Bite You' promises a mechanism (process explainer) not a list. No number, no superlative; the 😨 emoji supplies the emotion. Same family as the channel's 'What Happens When ...' / 'How X Works' Shorts. The script's first words literally restate the title ('When a horsefly bites you'), so title, first frame and first line all agree.

thumbnail.composition: No custom thumbnail: the yt-dlp maxres thumbnail is an auto-picked mid-video frame (~16 s, bursting blood vessel in pink tissue cross-section with caption 'until they burst') pillarboxed in a blurred 16:9 frame. In the Shorts feed the effective 'thumbnail' is the first frame: a photoreal 3D horsefly, centred, front-on, standing on a giant orange skin plane against a flat sky-blue gradient.
thumbnail.text: None designed. The burned-in caption ('When a horse fly' on frame 1; 'until they burst' on the auto thumb) is the only text, small white bold sans with dark shadow at ~78% height.
thumbnail.colours: First frame: saturated cyan/sky-blue background, warm orange-peach skin floor, near-black insect - strong complementary blue/orange split. Auto thumb: monochrome reds/pinks with a glowing orange-yellow highlighted vessel.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Insect rendered at human-head size against a horizon-flat skin 'landscape' - the macro-as-landscape trick makes a tiny fly read as a monster. At 1 s the camera reveals a whole man with the fly as a speck on his shoulder for the reverse scale hit.
thumbnail.why_it_works: For Shorts the first frame does the thumbnail's job: one recognisable, slightly gross subject, centred, high-contrast against a clean background, readable at feed size; no clutter. The topic (being bitten) is universal and visceral, so the title + creature is enough of a hook.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: When a horsefly bites you, it presses six needle-like tools against your skin.
hook.device: Instant cold open with zero preamble: the first line restates the title in second person ('When a horsefly bites you') and pays it off with a specific, surprising number + unsettling image ('six needle-like tools'). Visual scale whiplash in the first 2 s (macro fly -> whole man with fly as a speck -> back to fly) followed by a dive under the fly where six golden stylets fan out toward the camera. Body-horror curiosity: viewer's own skin is the stage.
hook.visual_0_5s: 0-0.9 s front-on CG horsefly on orange skin, sky-blue bg; 1.0-1.4 s cut to a 3D man in profile, fly tiny on his shoulder; 1.5-2 s back to fly; 2-4 s camera drops under the fly, six yellow/orange stylets fan out in extreme close-up; 4-4.5 s macro of compound eyes and red proboscis piercing skin.

beats.summary: 'When a horsefly bites you' - title said back as a second-person scenario over a macro fly, with a 1-frame-ish scale reveal of the whole person.
'it presses six needle-like tools against your skin' - number + weapon metaphor; camera dives under the fly to show six stylets fanning out, then piercing.
Two blades with sharp edges slice the skin 'like scissors' - skin plane morphs into a pink tissue cross-section, two blades scissor in, red pooling below.

Two more have 'tiny teeth like a saw' - blades briefly turn literal steel saw blades, then saw up and down, tearing a hole, rupturing a highlighted blood vessel 'until they burst and you start to bleed' (gore peak at ~16 s).
'Next, a hollow blade pumps in spit' - transition word 'Next'; hollow tube stylet seen end-on, white saliva droplet; macro of the cut glistening with saliva so it can't seal.
'so the blood keeps flowing out' - blood bead forms and swells along the cut line.

'as its spongy tip laps it up' - spongy labellum presses on the blood bead, cutaway of blood drawn up; ends on a wide fly-on-skin shot matching the opening frame so the Short loops seamlessly into 'When a horsefly bites you'. No CTA, no outro.

pacing.caption_chunk: 2-4 words per caption card, changes every ~0.5-1 s, synced to word timing
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: new visual idea every 1-2 s; a new analogy/escalation every ~4-5 s (scissors 7.5 s, saw 10.5 s, burst 16 s, spit 20 s, laps 26 s)
pacing.notes: One unbroken sentence chain: no pauses, no intro, no CTA. Continuous camera through one CG world (skin plane + sky) with morph transitions into cross-sections rather than hard cuts. Escalation ladder: press -> slice -> saw -> burst -> bleed -> spit -> lap. Ends mid-motion on a shot that matches frame 1 so viewers re-watch (loop).

techniques_worth_copying: Title restated as line 1 in second person ('When a X [does thing] you') - zero setup, the viewer is the victim from frame 1.

Specific counted inventory as the hook payoff ('six needle-like tools') then enumerate them in pairs (two... two more... a hollow one... spongy tip) - a built-in progress bar that keeps people for the next item.
One everyday-tool analogy per mechanism (scissors, saw, pump/spit, sponge) and SHOW the analogy literally for ~1 s (blades turn into steel saw blades).

Macro-as-landscape staging: a flat skin floor plane to the horizon and a flat sky-blue backdrop make an insect look monster-sized; one quick wide shot of the whole human gives the reverse scale shock.
Morph from surface view into a cross-section cutaway instead of cutting - keeps continuity and shows 'inside you'.
Glowing yellow highlight on the part being named (vessel, hollow stylet, teeth) - colour-coded attention pointer, no arrows or labels needed.
Escalating body-horror verbs (presses, slice, saw, tear, burst, bleed, laps) with a gore peak at ~60% runtime.
Seamless loop: last shot matches first shot and last clause flows grammatically into the first line; no outro/CTA, under 30 s.
Captions: small 2-4 word white bold sans with soft dark shadow at ~78% height, no karaoke highlight - unobtrusive so the visual carries.

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: Medium. The look is photoreal 3D (Blender-style) which pure SVG cannot match; the structure, pacing, scale tricks and cross-section storytelling are fully reproducible in a stylised flat/2.5D vector style.
assets: Parametric SVG insect (body, head with compound-eye pattern, legs, mouthpart group whose stylets can fan out/retract individually)
Skin 'ground plane' with perspective (CSS 3D or a skewed gradient polygon) + scattered hair strokes, sky-blue radial gradient backdrop
Simple human silhouette/profile for the scale-reveal shot
Cross-section tissue panel: layered SVG (epidermis red band, pink dermis with noise/turbulence filter texture, vessel tube)
Blade components: smooth blade, serrated blade (path generator for teeth), steel-saw skin variant, hollow tube with end-cap opening
Fluid FX: blood bead that grows (metaball via feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix goo filter), saliva droplet/bubbles, vessel burst particles
motion_systems: Virtual camera (scale/translate/rotate of a world group with spring easing) for push-ins, under-fly dives and pull-back loop
Morph transition surface -> cross-section (clip-path wipe or flubber path interpolation)
Highlight pulse (glow filter + colour lerp to yellow) bound to caption words
Sawing oscillation and tear-hole growth (animated path/mask)
Loop matcher: last frame composition identical to first
code_only_remake_requirements.audio_captions: Local TTS (Kokoro) at ~175 wpm, word timestamps from TTS or faster-whisper; caption component chunking 2-4 words at bottom-third, white bold with shadow.
code_only_remake_requirements.effort_estimate: ~15-20 storyboard shots per 30 s; reusable 'creature attacks you' kit (creature + skin plane + cross-section + fluids) would serve a whole series (mosquito, tick, leech, bed bug).
